title: Chapter 292: A Miracle Draw?
html:
Cold rain slipped beneath Chen Ge’s collar. Standing at the orchard’s edge, he stared at the message on his phone. A new option had appeared among the available Trial Missions—Coffin Village.

A three-star scenario is still too difficult for me. The Third Sick Hall is also a three-star scenario. Without Zhang Ya, I would have died then.

A three-star rating meant the scenario might contain more than one Red Specter. As far as Chen Ge knew, only another Red Specter posed a meaningful threat to one.

A Trial Mission from the black phone is never merely a mission. I have to account for its real-world consequences and what follows afterward. I can’t rush this. Chen Ge hesitated. I have a week to decide. Perhaps Zhang Ya will awaken within a few days. If she does, I can accept without hesitation.

He came to the decision and glanced at his shadow before shoving the phone into his pocket. I’ll decide in five days.

Coffin Village offered another option, but nothing compelled him to choose it immediately. Jiang Ling and Zhu Xinrou’s history suggested that the three-star mission could be every bit as dangerous as the Third Sick Hall. More importantly, the settlement at the mountain’s foot was Lin Guan Village, while the black phone named the mission location Coffin Village. Based on Master Bai’s account, the true destination was probably the mysterious settlement hidden deep in the mountains.

If unlocked, such a scenario would become a major Haunted House attraction. Few competitors could offer an entire abandoned haunted village, and the novelty would draw countless visitors. Chen Ge was undeniably tempted, but remained cautious.

Coffin Village lay deep in the mountains, far from civilization and probably beyond cellular coverage. If danger found him there, even escaping would be difficult.

The villagers of Coffin Village are born with abnormalities, and each family prepares a living coffin. This place is probably hiding plenty of monsters. Those who escaped to Bai Family Village looked normal, but their attitude toward those with abnormalities was curious. It was like they wanted to kill all of them.

Why did these people escape from the mountains? Was it really because of an epidemic?

Chen Ge could not understand why, but he was certain of one thing. Before entering Coffin Village, he needed to make friends with Jiang Ling. The girl was definitely not as innocent as she looked.

Both Yin Xiaoxiao and Fan Yu seem to like me. Perhaps I’m more natural around children than adults. It shouldn’t be too hard to make friends with Jiang Ling.

Peach trees rustled in the darkness. Master Bai gently widened the hollow beneath the fallen tree with his hoe, guilt etched into his features.

When Chen Ge offered to help, Master Bai refused. Chen Ge removed his jacket and draped it over a low branch to shield the body from the rain. As Master Bai cleared away the soil, the corpse began to slide free. The sight of the small arms growing beneath Zhu Xinrou’s normal pair left Chen Ge heartsick. She had been born this way; why had everyone blamed her for something beyond her control?

He remembered the childhood Master Bai had described. Regardless of the weather, Zhu Xinrou had been bundled in layers. Once others discovered her body, she endured their bullying and ridicule, forced to apologize for something she could not control.

She must have loved the winter when she was young.

The sight of Zhu Xinrou’s full body defied description. Yet Chen Ge felt no disgust or revulsion, only pity. He had encountered too many monsters—and too many monstrous people—to judge her by appearance alone.

“It’s not your fault.”

Chen Ge stood facing the wind to block the rain that threatened to pour into the hole.

The black phone vibrated again. Its message announced that Zhu Xinrou’s affinity toward him had risen from Stranger to Slightly Favorable.

Xiaoxiao held the same opinion of me when we first met. It seems Zhu Xinrou will no longer attack me without cause.

Without a taxi, leaving the isolated Lin Guan Village in the middle of the night was difficult, but Chen Ge already had a plan.

…

At 3:15 a.m., the police reached the orchard. As the person who discovered the body, Chen Ge asked to accompany them to the station and give a statement. By 5:30 a.m., he and Master Bai were sitting in Inspector Lee’s office.

Unlike the nervous Master Bai, Chen Ge remained relaxed; he had even slept briefly in the police car.

“Master Bai, tell them the truth and don’t be afraid. Jiujiang’s police are among the best; they won’t make trouble for you without cause.”

When Inspector Lee entered, Chen Ge was coaching Master Bai on speaking to the police with the confidence of a seasoned informant. Inspector Lee hardly knew how to react. “With every passing day, this kid behaves more like he works for us.”

“Uncle San Bao!” Chen Ge rose at the sight of him. “Sorry to trouble you again. A police officer’s work is never finished, is it?”

The old man beside him nodded. He was an honest man. He realized that they had reported the case in the middle of the night, and the police officers had trekked into the mountain before daylight. They were indeed hardworking. “Thank you for all the trouble you’ve gone through, sir.”

“It’s our duty.” Inspector Lee smiled at Master Bai, then turned to Chen Ge. “Jiujiang is enormous. Could you wander into another district once in a while? I’m begging you—take a vacation somewhere outside our jurisdiction. Give yourself a rest and give us one too.”

“Inspector Lee, you’re too kind. Don’t worry—my body can handle it.” Inspector Lee looked ready to stand and smack him, but restrained himself in front of Master Bai.

Inspector Lee rubbed his temples. After taking their statements, he quickly summoned Da Yong to escort Chen Ge out. Dark circles ringed Da Yong’s eyes as he walked him to the door and gripped his shoulder. “Brother, Inspector Lee speaks bluntly, so don’t take it personally. But if you don’t want a vacation, could you at least stay home and rest for a few days?”

Da Yong’s concern was genuine. Accepting the Western Jiujiang police station’s kindness, Chen Ge nodded solemnly. “All right. I’ll do my best.”

Chen Ge took a taxi back to New Century Park as the sun crested the horizon. Standing before the Haunted House in the newborn light, he suddenly drew out the black phone.

My midday draws have never gone particularly well. They say a good morning is the beginning of everything. Perhaps drawing now will bring better luck.

After a moment’s consideration, Chen Ge spent one hundred screams and spun the Wheel of Misfortune.
